# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 32 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Prologue and Saying 1

**1** These are the secret sayings that the living Jesus spoke and Didymos Judas Thomas wrote down.

**2** And he said: "Whoever finds the interpretation of these sayings will not taste death."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** Coptic ms. c. 340 CE; Greek Vorlage attested in P.Oxy 654 (lines 1-5), which preserves the prologue in nearly identical form.

**Reading adopted:** "Secret sayings" (EMET/LOGOS) preferred over PNEUMA's "hidden sayings" — *ехнт* carries the sense of something deliberately concealed, awaiting discovery by the worthy seeker.

**"The living Jesus"** — consensus holds this as a theological title present in both Coptic and Greek witnesses. PNEUMA's dash-rendering is explanatory but loses the nominal flow.

**"Finds the interpretation"** — all agents agree on "interpretation" (*херменеіа*). PNEUMA's "unlocks the meaning" is vivid but paraphrastic.

**"Shall not taste death"** — LOGOS and EMET preserve the Semitic idiom; PNEUMA's "never die" is accurate but loses the idiomatic flavor shared with John 8:52 and Mark 9:1.

**Synoptic Parallels:** The immortality promise has no direct Synoptic parallel but cf. John 8:51 ("whoever keeps my word will never see death") and John 11:26. The framing as a "sayings collection" is unique to Thomas in the canonical/near-canonical tradition.

**Theological Note:** The prologue sets up the entire collection as an interpretive challenge. Life is not given through belief or ritual but through the labor of understanding. This is the foundational claim of the Gospel of Thomas.
